chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, that he said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, I have been compelled to ask you.' He said, 'Ask.' I said, 'Sa'd ibn Sa'd has left a will that 'perform Hajj on my behalf,' but vaguely, and he did not specify anything, and we do not know how to do that.' He said, 'Hajj is performed on his behalf as long as he has wealth.'

key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ: Sa'd ibn Sa'd (the specific deceased person mentioned)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a deceased person's will vaguely instructs to perform Hajj on their behalf without specifying details?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the ambiguity of Sa'd ibn Sa'd's will regarding Hajj is resolved by establishing that a general command to 'perform Hajj for me' is legally sufficient to be executed from the deceased's estate. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that unspecified bequests for obligatory acts are fulfilled using available assets, ensuring the deceased's spiritual debts are settled without requiring further clarification from heirs.
